title: Free-variable count as a sum of indicators
statement:
Let $\rho$ be a restriction on $n$ variables, and let $U \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}$ be a set of indices. Then the number of indices in $U$ at which $\rho$ is free (unset), viewed as a real number, equals
\[
\abs{U \cap J} = \sum_{i \in U} \mathbf{1}[\rho(i)\ \text{is free}],
\]
where $J$ is the set of free variables of $\rho$ and each summand is $1$ when $\rho(i)$ is unset and $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: U is a finite set of indices in Fin n
ρ is a restriction on n variables
